subject: Short retention window request from Curie Health — follow-up & internal ask
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Morgan <aisha.morgan@curiehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Curie call recap — retention / PII asks + proposed next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and what we need from you to qualify the request for a shortened/zero-retention path: 

Call recap (high level)
- Curie wants to avoid persisting raw free-text that may contain PHI/PII and is asking whether we can support a 0-retention option for those inputs.
- They are open to a short metadata-only window for debugging / routing (they mentioned up to 7 days), but want explicit guarantees around PII removal.
- Residency: preferred US-East for initial pilots.

Open items / asks from Curie for Redwood:
1) Confirmation whether Redwood can support a technical pattern that guarantees PII is never stored in plaintext (client-side redaction, server-side redaction, or tokenization).
2) Evidence / artifacts: sample redaction design, SOC 2 or audit report, and a written exception path for short windows.
3) Proposed pilot timeline and what engineering effort is needed from Curie.

Proposed next steps (quick):
- I can share our redaction approach doc and a matrix of retention options (attached).
- If you confirm the desired policy (0-retention for content + 7-day metadata), we can scope a 2-week PoC to validate telemetry and audit logs with obfuscation.

Attachments: redaction-approach.pdf (high-level), retention-option-matrix.xlsx

If you can reply with the exact policy you want (i.e., "no raw text persisted, 7d non-PII metadata only, US-East"), I will route this to security/legal and create a short mutual action plan (MAP) and timeline.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Aisha Morgan <aisha.morgan@curiehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lahti <tom.lahti@curiehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Curie call recap — retention / PII asks + proposed next steps

Thanks Jonas — helpful recap. Confirming Curie's position: 
- Primary objective: prevent retention of free-text containing PHI. We need a contractual and technical commitment that plaintext PHI is not stored.
- Acceptable compromise: 0-retention of free-text inputs (we'd prefer this), with a short-lived window for non-PII metadata (we discussed 72 hours during the call; we are willing to consider up to 7 days but would like the shortest workable window).
- Residency: US-East acceptable for now.

What we will provide: sample redaction rules and a short list of high-risk fields our product populates. We'll also attach our data-requirements document so you can map controls to it (attached).

What we need from Redwood before committing to a PoC: 
1) A written description of the redaction approach you propose (client-side vs server-side) and any limitations.
2) A clear fallback plan if redaction fails (e.g., automated discard + alerting).
3) Confirmation that audit logs can be provided in an obfuscated form for compliance reviews.

Sidenote: Our legal team will want a short exception clause for the pilot that limits retention and prohibits reuse of retained artifacts.

Attach: curie_data_requirements.pdf

Appreciate the quick turn — Aisha
Aisha Morgan
Head of Product Operations, Curie Health
aisha.morgan@curiehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — Curie Health retention ask (options + legal considerations)

Jonas / Ben — looping in a quick internal summary and suggested path. I skimmed Curie's requirements and their attached document. Key legal/security points: 
- They want contractual language preventing retention of plaintext PHI and an exception clause for a PoC. Legal will require a mitigations matrix.
- They asked for "evidence": we should be ready to provide SOC 2 attestation (we have this), a redaction design doc that details where in the pipeline PII is detected and removed, and an audit log design that shows obfuscated IDs only.

Technical options to propose (pros/cons):
1) Client-side redaction (Curie removes PII before sending). Pros: strongest guarantee, low risk. Cons: requires engineering work on Curie's side and may miss edge cases.
2) Server-side deterministic redaction/tokenization (Redwood detects and strips PII at ingress). Pros: minimal customer work; Cons: detection gaps, must show high recall.
3) Hybrid: client-side redaction + server-side validation + ephemeral KV (7d or configurable short window). This is the most pragmatic for sales.

Recommendation: offer the hybrid as the default pilot: client-side redaction where possible, Redwood will perform server-side validation and keep only hashed IDs/metadata for up to 72 hours (we can offer 7 days as alternate). Provide an attestation packet and a short MAP.

Action items:
- Jonas: can you draft the MAP and the proposed pilot timeline for Aisha (include security questionnaire link and SOC 2).
- Ben: please confirm whether we can produce obfuscated audit logs and the retention TTL on KV caches (72h prototype vs 7d GA).

Attaching suggested retention-option-matrix.xlsx for discussion.

Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Morgan <aisha.morgan@curiehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Curie call recap — retention / PII asks + proposed next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks, and appreciate the data requirements file. Based on your ask and our internal discussion, here is a concrete proposal to move to a PoC quickly: 

Proposal (PoC)
- Pattern: Client-side redaction + Redwood server-side validation. Curie will send redacted payloads; Redwood will run a verification pass and will not persist raw text if PII markers are present.
- Retention window: Redwood will keep only obfuscated metadata and hashed IDs for 72 hours by default for debugging. We can extend to 7 days if needed, but will document the change in the MAP.
- Residency: US-East; logs and any temporary KV are stored in the requested region.
- Audit logs: Redwood can provide obfuscated audit logs (timestamp + hashed request id + action taken). We will not include user-submitted free text in those artifacts.

Next steps / timeline
1) Redwood shares SOC 2 attestation and the redaction-approach doc (attached).
2) Curie shares final redaction rules and a set of synthetic examples we can use for validation.
3) Security questionnaire: I will send the link to our shared security questionnaire and the MAP (we'll add a 30-day pilot scope and an exception clause limiting retention to the pilot window).
4) PoC timeline: kickoff within 5 business days after legal ok; 2-week engineering validation; 2-week joint review and acceptance.

If that sounds reasonable, I will prepare the MAP and a short one-page exception addendum for the pilot for legal review. Ben / Marissa — please confirm OK on obfuscated logs + 72h TTL and I'll finalize the language for Aisha.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Curie-PoC-plan (PoC doc), HubSpot HS-Deal-4921

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
